page.description: antiX editions and architectures: compare, download official images, or prepare a USB with ROMinit CLI.
page.intro: A lean Debian-based desktop for old machines, with five init systems and no systemd. Pick the full desktop or the smaller core image, then the architecture.
pros: Runs on very little: core fits a 256 MB machine with swap.
Five init systems to choose from, and no systemd or elogind.
Debian 13 base with the project's own live-USB tooling.
Full and core flavours for both 64-bit and 32-bit machines.
cons: The look is dated and the defaults are spartan.
The project publishes no end-of-life date, so support is best-effort.
Full and core images differ by more than size: core needs you to add a desktop.
The only Commons screenshot shows a 2010 release, not 26.1.
page.previewNote: A stock screenshot of antiX from 2010, from Wikimedia Commons. It is not 26.1 and not a ROMinit recording: no image was written to a USB stick and nothing was booted for this page.

page.status: Two paths: the full desktop ISO or the smaller core ISO, written with dd or any image writer. Writing erases the stick; the live system installs to the disk you choose.
